sources.title: Stefan Adams, Mathematical Statistical Mechanics, MPI Lecture Note 30
sources.locator: Complete 98-page lecture-note PDF read; §5.2, Theorem 5.3 and its complete proof, printed pp.37–41.

contents.name: Stability bound in the hypotheses of Theorem 5.3
contents.support: The stability lower bound is the same finite-configuration condition; the local model separately states its Borel, power-tail, and unrestricted-core scope.

contents.name: Theorem 5.3: canonical free-energy limit under its strong-tempering and sign hypotheses
contents.reason: The local claim is a grand-canonical free-cube limit for a two-sided power tail and unrestricted positive core; Theorem 5.3 has different ensemble and potential hypotheses.

sources.title: M. E. Fisher and J. L. Lebowitz, Asymptotic Free Energy of a System with Periodic Boundary Conditions
sources.locator: Complete original paper read; §§II–III and VI, printed pp.252–271.

contents.name: Stability condition for the finite-volume pair energy, §§II–III
contents.support: The local model records the same uniform lower bound on every finite pair configuration and states its separate power-tail condition.

contents.name: Periodic-boundary canonical free-energy comparison, §§II–III
contents.reason: Those sections address periodic-boundary canonical free energy under different interaction assumptions; the assigned claim is free-boundary grand pressure and is proved locally.

contents.name: Grand-canonical pressure treatment, §VI
contents.support: Section VI is an abbreviated treatment under hard-core and weak-tempering hypotheses; it is used only for comparison while the assigned proof supplies the full power-tail block argument.

sources.title: D. Ruelle, Classical Statistical Mechanics of a System of Particles
sources.locator: Complete 16-page PDF read; Properties A and F, with the original p.184 formulas visually checked.

contents.name: Thermodynamic-limit result for the paper’s decomposable positive-type radial interactions
contents.reason: The paper imposes a restricted three-dimensional radial positive-type/decomposable class, so it does not supply the assigned theorem for general stable power-tempered pair potentials.

sources.title: Terence Tao, 245A Notes 3: Integration on Abstract Measure Spaces and the Convergence Theorems
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML lecture text read; nonnegative integral definition by simple minorants and the convergence-theorems section.

contents.name: Definition of the nonnegative integral as a supremum over simple minorants
contents.support: The local bridge identifies the exact simple-minorant class and compares the same level-set integral values before taking suprema.

sources.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory Notes, Chapter 4: Integration
sources.locator: Chapter 4, §§4.1–4.2, pp.39–42; the complete relevant sections on simple and nonnegative integrals read.

contents.name: Definition 4.1: integral of a nonnegative simple function, including 0·∞=0
contents.support: The local bridge checks that both definitions assign the same finite level-set sum with the same zero-times-infinity convention.

contents.name: Definition 4.4: nonnegative integral as a supremum over simple minorants
contents.support: This is the exact shared interface whose simple-minorant classes and values the local bridge equates.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3: linearity, positivity, and monotonicity for simple integrals
contents.support: The cutoff proof uses only monotonicity from the local supremum definition and gives that comparison directly.

contents.name: Proposition 4.5: homogeneity and monotonicity for nonnegative integrals
contents.support: The cutoff estimate uses monotonicity of a nonnegative integral; the local proof derives it by inclusion of simple-minorant classes.
